scheme_name: Civil Service Incentive (De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-nomadic communities )
description:
The Civil Service Incentive Scheme for De-Notified, Nomadic, and Semi-nomadic Communities was launched by the Government of India in 2021. 

This scheme aims to promote the inclusion of marginalized communities in civil services. 

The scheme specifically targets the De-Notified, Nomadic, and Semi-nomadic communities, which have historically faced social and economic disadvantages. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance and support to eligible candidates from these communities to prepare for civil service examinations. 

The scheme intends to enhance the representation of these communities in various government positions. 

The government has set a measurable target of increasing the participation of these communities in civil services by 10 percent over the next five years. 

The scheme offers financial assistance of up to INR 1 lakh per candidate. 

This financial support can be utilized for purchasing study materials, enrolling in coaching classes, and covering examination fees. 

Additionally, the scheme provides scholarships for candidates who successfully qualify for the preliminary examination. 

The scholarship amount is INR 25,000 for those who clear the preliminary stage and proceed to the main examination. 

Eligibility for the scheme is strictly defined. 

Candidates must belong to the De-Notified, Nomadic, or Semi-nomadic communities as recognized by the Government of India. 

The age limit for applicants is set at 21 to 35 years. 

Candidates must also possess at least a graduate degree from a recognized university. 

Income criteria stipulate that the annual family income should not exceed INR 8 lakh. 

The application process is straightforward and involves several steps. 

Interested candidates must fill out the application form available on the official government website. 

The application form requires personal details, educational qualifications, and community certificates. 

Candidates must attach a copy of their family income certificate. 

Additionally, a copy of the educational qualification certificate is required. 

Once the application form is completed, candidates must submit it online before the deadline. 

The deadline for application submissions is typically set for the end of March each year. 

After submission, the applications are reviewed by the designated authorities. 

Candidates are notified of the status of their applications within two months of the deadline. 

Disbursement of funds occurs in two phases. 

The first phase involves the release of INR 1 lakh for eligible candidates upon approval of their applications. 

The second phase involves the scholarship amount of INR 25,000, which is disbursed after candidates clear the preliminary examination. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

The ministry has established a dedicated helpline for queries related to the scheme. 

The contact number for the helpline is 1800 180 2000. 

The scheme has been well-received, with over 5,000 applications submitted in its first year. 

Feedback from beneficiaries indicates that the financial assistance has significantly eased their preparation for civil services. 

The government aims to expand the scheme to include additional support services in the coming years. 

This includes mentorship programs and workshops to enhance candidates' skills. 

The scheme aligns with the broader goals of the Government of India to promote social equity and inclusion. 

It is part of a series of initiatives aimed at empowering marginalized communities. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 50 crores for the initial rollout of the scheme. 

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme's effectiveness will be conducted annually. 

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment will publish an annual report detailing the progress and outcomes of the scheme. 

This report will include statistics on the number of beneficiaries, success rates in civil service examinations, and feedback from participants. 

The scheme also encourages partnerships with non-governmental organizations for outreach and support. 

These partnerships are intended to raise awareness about the scheme among the targeted communities. 

The government is committed to ensuring that the benefits reach the intended recipients effectively. 

In conclusion, the Civil Service Incentive Scheme for De-Notified, Nomadic, and Semi-nomadic Communities represents a significant step towards inclusivity in civil services. 

By providing financial assistance and support, the scheme aims to empower marginalized communities. 

It seeks to create a more equitable representation in government positions. 

The comprehensive structure of the scheme ensures that eligible candidates receive the necessary resources to succeed. 

The government's commitment to monitoring and evaluating the scheme will help in making necessary adjustments for future improvements. 

Overall, this initiative reflects the ongoing efforts of the Indian government to uplift and empower underrepresented communities in the civil service sector.
